questions.q: What is the simple formula used to calculate the speed of a moving object?
questions.a: Speed = Distance / Time. A student who answers "Distance times Time" is confusing the concept of rate with total accumulation, showing they haven't grasped that speed is a division of distance into time intervals.

questions.q: If two cars travel the same distance, but Car A takes 10 minutes and Car B takes 20 minutes, which car is faster and why?
questions.a: Car A is faster because it covered the same distance in less time. A student who says "they are the same" likely ignores the role of time in the definition of speed, focusing only on the fact that the distance travelled was identical.

questions.q: A student walks a 20-metre corridor in 5 seconds. Calculate the speed of the student.
questions.a: Speed = 20 m / 5 s = 4 m/s. A student who performs 20 x 5 = 100 or 5 / 20 = 0.25 m/s has not correctly applied the division order of the speed formula.

questions.q: Why do we say that speed tells us about the "rate" of motion?
questions.a: It describes how distance changes for every one unit of time (like a second or an hour). A student who simply says "it shows how fast" lacks the analytical link between the variable of distance and the variable of time.

questions.q: If a cyclist travels at a constant speed, does that mean they have stopped moving? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, constant speed means they are covering the same amount of distance in every equal interval of time. A student who believes constant speed means "at rest" is confusing a steady motion with a zero-motion state.

questions.q: Create a scenario where you would need to measure speed in your daily life.
questions.a: A good answer involves timing a trip to a local shop, like: "I want to know my speed to the vegetable market, so I measure the path is 500 metres and it takes me 200 seconds." A poor answer would be vague, like "measuring a car," without explaining the need for both distance and time measurements.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Speed is a measure of how quickly an object covers a ______ distance over a period of time.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you and your ______ decide to race from the school gate to the playground.
What is Speed? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Speed is a measure of how quickly an object covers a specific distance over a period of time.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Speed?
questions.a: Students often believe that "speed" and "distance" are the same thing.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to calculate the speed of an object given its distance and time, identify the correct units, and explain what a higher or lower speed value signifies in a real-world scenario.
